financials_interim.notes: Hayleys Fabric PLC reports its primary/functional-currency financial statements in USD (unit_scale='1', i.e. full USD amounts, not thousands) -- the LKR figures on pages 10-12 of the filing are an explicitly-labelled 'for convenience purposes only' translation and are NOT used here, to avoid mixing two currency bases within one row and because the cash-flow statement is NOT translated to LKR in this filing (only the P&L and balance sheet are). No 'operating profit' subtotal is presented by the company; operating_profit here = Gross Profit + Other operating income - Administrative expenses - Distribution expenses - Other expenses, which reconciles to the disclosed PBT after deducting 'Net financing expense' to within $1 (rounding). The filing discloses only a single net 'Net financing expense' line (not split gross finance income/finance costs): for GROUP this was a net expense (151,705) so it is recorded under finance_costs with finance_income left blank; for COMPANY it was a net income (44,022) so it is recorded under finance_income with finance_costs left blank. Balance-sheet identity (total assets = total liabilities + total equity) ties out exactly for both GROUP and COMPANY as at 30.06.2026 and 30.06.2025. EPS cross-check (PAT attributable to owners / 415,481,776 shares in issue) matches the disclosed Basic/Diluted EPS of USD 0.001 (Group) and USD 0.002 (Company). No column-swap issues were found.

interim_updates.note_text: Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026), Group basis, all figures in USD. Revenue fell 5.1% YoY to USD 32.71mn (32,705,222) from USD 34.46mn (34,461,631), while cost of sales fell only 3.6% (27,386,498 vs 28,424,697), compressing gross margin to 16.3% from 17.5% and gross profit -11.9% (5,318,724 vs 6,036,934). Administrative expenses rose 12.6% to USD 3.82mn (3,815,064 vs 3,387,104). These pressures were partly offset by net financing expense falling 76.5% to USD 151,705 from USD 647,047 (the filing discloses only a single net financing line, not gross finance income/costs), leaving PBT down a milder 37.3% at USD 1,226,307 (vs 1,955,238). PAT fell much further, -60.9% to USD 506,132 (vs 1,294,755), because income tax expense actually rose 9.0% to USD 720,175 (vs 660,483) despite lower pre-tax profit -- the effective tax rate roughly doubled to ~58.7% from ~33.8%. On a Company (standalone) basis revenue fell 8.8% to USD 20.62mn (vs 22.61mn) and PAT fell 46.9% to USD 631,474 (vs 1,189,861); the Company's net financing line swung from a USD 306,764 net expense to a USD 44,022 net income, cushioning its PBT decline to -31.8% versus the larger revenue/gross-profit fall. Directors declared a first interim dividend of Rs 0.11/share (Rs.45.70mn) on 30 June 2026, paid 21 July 2026.

interim_updates.takeaway: Group PBT fell 37.3% YoY largely on gross-margin compression (cost of sales did not fall as fast as revenue) partially offset by a 76.5% drop in net financing expense; but PAT fell much further (-60.9%) because the effective tax rate roughly doubled to ~59% from ~34% -- a swing not explained by the operating figures alone and worth flagging for follow-up.
operational_highlights: Group gross margin compressed to 16.3% from 17.5% as cost of sales fell only -3.6% against a -5.1% revenue decline
Group administrative expenses rose +12.6% to USD 3.82mn (3,815,064 vs 3,387,104)
Group net financing expense fell 76.5% to USD 151,705 from USD 647,047, cushioning the PBT decline
Group effective tax rate rose sharply to ~58.7% (tax USD 720,175 on PBT USD 1,226,307) from ~33.8% a year earlier, driving PAT down -60.9% even though PBT fell only -37.3%
First interim dividend of Rs 0.11/share (Rs.45.70mn) declared 30 June 2026, paid 21 July 2026
key_drivers: Cost of sales (knitted fabric manufacturing input costs) did not fall in step with revenue, compressing gross margin from 17.5% to 16.3% -- points to pricing/volume pressure rather than cost relief
Administrative expenses up 12.6% YoY partially offset the benefit of the lower net financing expense
The steep rise in the effective tax rate (~33.8% -> ~58.7%) is the single biggest driver of the -60.9% PAT decline versus the milder -37.3% PBT decline
